rationale: Internally consistent and economically coherent (EBITDA/EV cheapness gated by EBIT/assets), but it is essentially the well-trodden value×operating-profitability composite and shares the archive's already-tested cheapness×profitability architecture, so novelty is limited even if the depreciation-adjustment framing is defensible.

Book-to-market conditioned on the three-year *worst-case* after-interest operating profitability is a genuinely distinct construction (a solvency floor rather than an average quality level), the expression matches the hypothesis, and it plausibly separates solvent value from distressed value without merely re-scoring an F-score.

The penalty term |oancf − oiadp|/at is not an accrual-quality or "corroboration" measure as claimed — because oiadp is post-depreciation, the gap is dominated by depreciation and taxes, so the signal mechanically penalizes capital-intensive and high-tax-rate firms, making the stated mechanism inconsistent with what the expression computes.

This is a near-rediscovery of the archived "Expensive Fragile-Margin Penalty" — identical sales-multiple and MA(gross margin)−VOL(gross margin) ingredients with only the aggregator flipped from MAX to MUL and the volatility window shortened, which is precisely the cosmetic-variant path the objective warns against.

Pairing cash-flow yield with a declining SG&A-to-sales trend introduces a genuinely forward-looking cost-discipline channel that does not algebraically collapse into another current profit yield, though the tester should be alert that falling SG&A/sales can reflect either efficiency gains or cuts to intangible investment (which literature associates with *lower* future returns), which could blunt the expected positive sign.

The within-firm valuation-dislocation idea is legitimately novel relative to the archive, but TS_RANK over a 3-period annual window admits only three distinct values, so the value leg degenerates into a coarse, lumpy tercile indicator that will destabilize portfolio composition and waste most of the cross-sectional information — extend the window or use a normalized deviation from the firm's own trailing mean instead.
